thread.title: Dow Turns Higher, Nasdaq Reverses Losses - TheStreet

author: thestreet.com
title: Dow Turns Higher, Nasdaq Reverses Losses - TheStreet
text:
Here Are 4 Hot Things to Know About Stocks Right Now The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell back into correction territory on Tuesday after dropping 1.4%, or 345 points. The blue-chip Dow has declined 3.5% so far in 2018. If it closes lower in the first quarter, a nine-quarter streak of gains will end. The Dow was on pace for its worst month of trading since January 2016. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell nearly 3% on Tuesday but has risen 1.5% year to date. Wall Street Overview U.S. stocks were higher on Wednesday, March 28, with tech stocks reversing earlier losses and rebounding from a major selloff in the previous session.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 127 points, or 0.53%, to 23,984, the S&P 500 gained 0.47%, and the Nasdaq gained 0.23%. Tech shares such as Twitter Inc. ( TWTR )  , Facebook Inc.  ( FB )   , Google parent Alphabet Inc.  ( GOOGL )  , Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA )  , Netflix Inc. ( NFLX )  and Apple Inc. ( AAPL )  registered significant declines on Tuesday, March 27, pulling broader markets to the downside.
Facebook rose nearly 2% on Wednesday after the social media giant said it was overhauling its security and privacy settings following the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN ) fell 4% on a report that Donald Trump wants to go after the online retailing giant . 
Facebook, Alphabet, Nvidia, Apple and Amazon are holdings in Jim Cramer's Action Alerts PLUS Charitable Trust Portfolio. Want to be alerted before Cramer buys or sells the stocks?  Learn more now . 
The final estimate of gross domestic product in the fourth quarter was raised to a 2.9% annual rate, up from the prior estimate of 2.5%, the Commerce Department said Wednesday. GDP growth in the third quarter was 3.2%.
"So while there is no shortage of noise out there to distract investors, especially in light of the recent tech wreck and headwinds from a hawkish (Federal Reserve) ... upward revision (of GDP) should serve as a reminder that economic fundamentals carry weight and remain strong," said Mike Loewengart, vice president of investment strategy at E*Trade Financial Corp.
A federal appeals court overturned a decision in a long-running legal battle over whether Alphabet's Google infringed on Oracle Corp.'s ( ORCL ) Java programming language to build its Android mobile operating system. The court said Google's use of Java was "not fair" and sent the case back to trial to determine damages.
Oracle had originally sought $9 billion. The court said Android helped Google earn $42 billion in advertising revenue since the first Android phone went on sale in 2008, the Associated Press reported.
Oracle fell 0.15%, while Alphabet rose 1%.
Shares of Tesla Inc. ( TSLA ) fell 4.6% on Wednesday after the National Transportation Safety Board announced an investigation into a fatal crash involving one of the company's vehicles.
Meanwhile, Tesla had its credit rating downgraded  by Moody's Investors Service on Tuesday, with the ratings agency citing "significant shortfall" in the production of the Tesla Model 3, and warned warned that it faces "liquidity pressures due to its large negative cash flow and the pending maturities of convertible bonds."
Tesla Shares Hit One-Year Low as Safety, Liquidity Concerns Mount on Carmaker Shire Pharmaceuticals PLC  ( SHPG )  surged 18% Wednesday after Japan's Takeda Pharmaceutical Co. ( TKPYY )   confirmed that it was interested in making a bid for the British drugmaker.
Takeda, Japan's biggest drugmaker by sales, said Shire would bolster its core therapeutic areas of oncology, GI and neuroscience and align the company with market opportunities in the United States. It also noted value propositions in Shire's global rare disease franchise.
Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc. ( WBA ) posted adjusted earnings in its fiscal second quarter of $1.73 a share, higher than analysts' estimates of $1.55. Revenue was $33.02 billion, ahead of forecasts of $32.2 billion. The drugstore chain also raised its earnings guidance for 2018. The stock rose 1.8%.
BlackBerry Inc. ( BB ) shares jumped 2.3% after the software company posted  fiscal fourth-quarter earnings and sales that beat Wall Street expectations.
Lululemon Athletica Inc. gained 10.3% after the yoga-clothing retailer reported fourth-quarter profit and sales that topped estimates.
